en.sup: Supplied in English. The Hebrew sets 'our fields and our vineyards' after the rest with no preposition; most likely the land stood as security for the loan.

01.r: Introduces a second group among the complaining people.
01.n: The same opening as the verse before: a noun of existence, 'there is', used for the verb 'to be' without a tense of its own.

02.n: BDB notes that this particle can include its own antecedent, so 'who' here means 'those who'.

03.r: What this second group was saying.

04.n: Gesenius gives a first sense, to adhere or be joined closely, and from it to borrow, to receive as a loan. He compares the Latin nexus, a debtor bound over to his creditor.

05.r: Silver, the money of the loan.
05.n: Our register keeps 'silver' for this word where every translation here says 'money'. Gesenius: silver, so called from its pale colour; the brief's lexicon also gives money.

06.r: The payment owed to the king, which the loans were raised to meet.
06.n: Our data finds this word in this verse only. BDB gives 'tribute', and the brief's lexicon names an Aramaic word for tribute as its equivalent. Gesenius derives the noun from the root 'to measure', with first senses length and measure; that the tribute was a measured levy is a reasonable reading, not something the lexicons state.

07.r: The king to whom the tribute is due.

08.r: The land standing behind the loans.
08.n: There is no preposition before this word in the Hebrew; the translations supply 'upon' or 'on'.

09.r: Their vineyards, pledged with the fields.

_extra.15: καὶ (and): begins a phrase added in the Greek, 'and our houses'.
_extra.16: οἰκίαι (houses): the Greek adds houses to the fields and vineyards, as the verse before lists them; the Hebrew of this verse has none.
_extra.17: ἡμῶν (our): part of the added phrase.

04.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. Ἐδανισάμεθα, 'we borrowed', the middle of δανείζω, to lend.

05.n: ἀργύριον, silver, and so money: the word our register renders 'silver' in the New Testament.

06.n: εἰς φόρους, 'for tributes', plural. φόρος is the word our register renders 'tribute' in the New Testament.

08.n: The Greek has no 'on': 'our fields and our vineyards and our houses' stand as a list by themselves.
